quest.title: The Lonesome Euthymia
quest.description: Your adventure has come to an end for now. You and Paimon decide to pay the Statue of the Omnipresent God a visit...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x475, Mora x29525, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go to the Statue of the Omnipresent God
Talk to Thoma and Kujou Kamaji

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: If the Tenryou Commission won't assist in dealing with the thunderstorm, the consequences could be catastrophic.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: It's not that we're unwilling to do our part. We just don't have any spare hands right now. I hope you can understand.

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Exactly. So let's keep the discussion going, and see if we can find a solution.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Thoma! What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Ah, hello you two. We were just talking about what an impact you've made in Inazuma.

choices.text: What a coincidence.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Greetings. Thank you both again for delivering Miss Hiiragi's letter that time.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Ah, so they're friends of yours. I'm Master Kamaji's servant. Call me Ippei!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like you're having some trouble?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Well, the Tri-Commission's work used to consist of gathering information for the Shogun and carrying out any duties she assigned.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: But recently, she announced that she wishes to spend some time in solitude and self-reflection. Since she is refusing to receive any visitors, there is no one to tell us what to do.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: We all understand if the Shogun needs some quiet time to gather her thoughts. The only problem is, in the meantime, the thunderstorm out at sea has been getting wilder.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hear that storm represents the Shogun's will.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Yup, that's the one, and in all the time it's been there, the storm has never changed in shape or size. But now, it seems to be drawing closer to Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? So her will's changed and she wants to destroy Inazuma now? Or is this her way of trying to get revenge on us?

choices.text: That would be a little childish.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah, you're right. If she really wanted to get revenge on us, she could just strike us with lightning right here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Which would also be pretty scary!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, I don't think you need to worry about that. The reason we're concerned is that we've never known the Almighty Shogun's will to falter before.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Considering Liyue's god left not too long ago, it's hard not to take it as a bad sign.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: A lot of people now believe that the thunderstorm is getting wilder because the Almighty Shogun is having health problems. The fact that she won't see anyone right now makes us concerned that things are only going to get worse.

choices.text: That seems like a valid concern.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Right. So, before rumors start spreading, Miss Kamisato got me to come here and discuss countermeasures with the Tenryou Commission. We need to make sure we're prepared to deal with the chaos if and when it arrives.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Unfortunately, the reality is that the Tenryou Commission is facing huge internal instability at the moment. The Kujou Clan has lost control over the other clans.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why is that?

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: The Kujou Clan is still awaiting the Shogun's trial for colluding with the Fatui and nearly destroying the whole of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Everyone knows that a change of Commissioner is inevitable. It's just a matter of time before the Almighty Shogun hands down her decree.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: To put it simply, no one will take orders from the Kujou Clan anymore, but there's still work that has to be done.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: If Mr. Takayuki was in better health, there might be a way through. But now...

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: My lack of ability is to blame. I failed to uncover the truth in time, and I failed to stop my father. And now, as acting head of the clan, I'm failing to quell the unrest.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Don't blame yourself, Master. You have to at least keep your chin up until your older brother returns. The Kujou Clan can't cope with any more instability in its current state.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Yes, you're right. Masahito has enough on his plate at the moment. I mustn't cause any more issues for him.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Okay. Thoma, let's revisit this discussion in a few days. Right now, I need to go visit Takatsukasa Susumu, head of the Takatsukasa Clan. He is the only one capable of taking charge of the situation now.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hmmm...I suppose. Okay, no problem. A speedy resolution to the Tenryou Commission's internal issues is in our best interests as well.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: I'll come with you, Master!

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: No need. I'll handle this by myself.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Oh okay... take care, then. Come back soon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you think about it, both the thunderstorm situation and the issue with the Tenryou Commission have been caused by the Shogun's decision to take some time off, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If things carry on like this, people will start to panic...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe we could invite her out for a while?

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Huh? You can actually do that!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't know for sure, but we may as well try. Whether she takes us up on the offer or not will depend on what mood she's in...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Sounds like you guys know what to do. Shall I leave it up to you, then?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Everyone's worrying about the Shogun's condition, but if people got to see her in person, it would put their fears to rest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll try.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: #Thank you very much, {NICKNAME}. I owe you one, again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The way Paimon sees it, there's only one person who might have the chance to see the Shogun while she's isolating. Right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's take a trip to the Grand Narukami Shrine!

choices.text: There must be a reason for the change in the storm.
Are you really scared of her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nuh-uh, she lost to us. Paimon's not scared, why would Paimon be scared!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's just, y'know, a little... concerned that she might be angry. Yeah, that's all, just a little concerned.

choices.text: Are you mocking me?

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Narukami Shrine and look for Yae Miko

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Are you here to see Lady Yae?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: She was inside a moment ago, but her movements are always a source of mystery — you never know when she might disappear...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Anyway, you may head in and see if she's there.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I wasn't expecting to receive VIP shrine visitors during down time. Hehe, so I suppose you're here just to visit me?

choices.text: Yes, I was.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: What a smooth talker... though, your eyes do not lie as convincingly as your tongue. You came because you need my help, didn't you?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Still, your answer has put me in a good mood.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So, tell me. What is the matter?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We heard that the Shogun decided to take a break, and since then the thunderstorm around Inazuma has gotten wilder.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rumor has it that the thunderstorm is affected by the Shogun's will. So people are worrying that something might be wrong with her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Tenryou Commission also needs her attention.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright. There's little purpose in keeping anything hidden from you, anyway.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Since the battle, the Shogun has been greatly troubled and her temperament has changed drastically.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

choices.text: Her temperament has changed?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Her power was already on the decline. Then you dealt her that fateful strike.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The defeat was a heavy blow to her. It also didn't help that I forgot to bring her some Tricolor Dango and light novels when I went to see her...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, the poor thing. Without desserts and books to console herself with, she was so angry she quite simply lost it. Crying and ranting and raving... Oh, I could hardly bear to see her that way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You expect us to believe that a god would throw a temper tantrum over something like that!?

choices.text: I don't believe you.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe. Before you get too indignant, consider the fact that your concerns sound every bit as nonsensical to me as that blatant lie did to you.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ei seeks eternity. To her, mortal lives come and go in the blink of an eye. Of what consequence to her are mortal concerns for her wellbeing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're saying she's fine, right?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I don't know the details. She said she wanted to rest, and I have nothing pressing that requires her attention. So there is no reason to disturb her.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I have heard about the thunderstorm, though. As to the cause, it is not inconceivable that, as you suggest, her will has wavered somewhat.

choices.text: All the more reason to check on her.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I am the only one in all of Inazuma who can visit her while she is resting.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But tell me, why should this concern me? Why should I do this for you, when I already have everything one could ever want, and have seen everything one could ever wish to see?

choices.text: Do it for the people of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Haha. I like that answer.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Here is the Pass Permit. Show it to the Okuzumeshuu at the gate, and he will let you in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, Miko!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: My question was in jest, but since you answered it in earnest, please stay true to your word.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, and don't forget to return the Pass Permit to me after you have finished with it.

choices.text: Do it for Ei.
Maybe she's gone stir-crazy.
It's not beyond the realm of possibility.
That's hard to believe...
Actually, I wanted to ask you about something.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, how cold. I saved your skin, didn't I? Surely you could at least humor me by engaging in some small talk first?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Then again, I suppose your frankness is part of your charm.

talks.objective: Talk to Takeshi at the entrance

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: The Almighty Shogun has requested solitude. No visitors allowed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've got a Pass Permit from Miko.

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: Don't be ridiculous. Lady Guuji never gives her Pass Permit to another person, not even esteemed travelers like yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: Guuji Yae is only authorized to hold that Pass Permit because of the trust that the Almighty Shogun places in her and her alone...

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: Wait... This is... authentic!?

choices.text: It'd be a little difficult to forge it.

response.speaker: Takeshi
response.text: Understood. Then, as the Shogun has ordered, I must not stand in your way.

response.speaker: Takeshi
response.text: Apologies, please proceed. Since the Shogun is resting at this time, please be especially respectful and make sure your behavior is impeccable.

choices.text: Feel free to check with Miko.

talks.objective: Go to Tenshukaku to see the Shogun

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun
dialogues.text: How did you get in?

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun
dialogues.text: Trespassers are to be eliminated at once.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no, it's us! Why are you treating us like we're your enemies!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We made amends, didn't we? Also, we got in by totally legitimate means!

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun
dialogues.text: Denied. Use of force has been forbidden.

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun
dialogues.text: Anyway. Be gone. Do not disturb my solitude.

choices.text: Forbidden? Why?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: That is of no concern. This is my recuperation state.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh, {NICKNAME}, what do you make of this? She's acting strange, huh?

choices.text: Do puppets really need rest and relaxation?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: This body has no need of rest. But I am an assistant to the one within. If she wishes to rest, I must follow her will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it. So this is all Ei's doing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why? Surely you going about your business doesn't interfere with the Plane of Euthymia?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's got plenty of space in there. Seems like it would be the perfect place for rest and relaxation.

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: I do as she wishes. I can say no more than this.

choices.text: Why not put their minds at rest?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: I cannot. In my current state, even if I went out, I could do nothing.

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: I am currently unwilling to deal with any business. I am also incapable of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you mean by that?

response.speaker: Raiden Shogun
response.text: It has been forbidden. *sigh* Please refrain from making me talk any further.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What should we do, {NICKNAME}? It feels like this conversation is going nowhere.

choices.text: Are you sick?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Ah, it's you two. It's been a while.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Shogun can't do much at the moment. Come straight in and see me.

choices.text: Have you malfunctioned?
Everyone's worried and wants to see you.
Has she ever been like this before?
Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was terrifying! Would it be so hard to give us a little warning first...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: It's not your first time. I don't see what there is to be so alarmed about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, is the Shogun broken? Are you gonna get it fixed, or...?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Don't worry. The Shogun's not broken, I've just temporarily disabled many of her functions.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Currently, the Shogun is unable to handle any business and cannot appear as me. So the easiest solution was to announce that I am resting.

choices.text: That's what she meant by "forbidden"...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: As I said, I need to think about Inazuma's Eternity. And thinking takes time.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But the Shogun is still running based on her old rules. I can't allow her to make any more mistakes while I am working things out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have you tried turning it off and on again?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: No. She was not created to ever be turned off.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Furthermore, I had even predicted at the time that I may wish to modify the Shogun's operational rules at some point in the future. However, such changes would not be conducive to Eternity.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You are so strict with yourself...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: That's why the Shogun has a robust system to safeguard against modification. It's also to protect against unforeseen circumstances.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: For now, while I figure out the form that Eternity should take, it's more effective for me to temporarily disable some of the puppet's functions rather than attempt to modify her rules.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it now. The thunderstorm's getting out of control because some of the Shogun's functions have been disabled.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The thunderstorm is getting out of control? This is the first I've heard of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Okay, well, let us bring you up to speed...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Hmm, I see. So the thunderstorm is drawing closer...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can fix it... right?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: It's just a minor error. This kind of thing was bound to happen. A small modification to the Shogun should fix it.

choices.text: ...So everyone was worked up over nothing.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Don't look at me like that. I've never had to tinker with the Shogun before, and she's very complicated. It's practically inevitable for something to go wrong when you start tweaking things.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes, that's it. I'm not making excuses. It's the truth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's fine. Just as long as you can fix it is all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Any progress on your thoughts about Eternity?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Not much. As before, I can see the way forward, yet there are still contradictions.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But there is no urgency. To reach an ill-conceived verdict in haste, just for the sake of having reached one, would be a confusion of priorities.

choices.text: Come with us. Get a change of pace.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If everyone sees that the Shogun is in good health, it'll put all the speculation and rumors out there to rest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And who knows, a change of scenery might put you in a different mood and give you some fresh inspiration!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: You mean... leave the Plane of Euthymia?

choices.text: It might do everyone some good.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes, you're right. After all, the Shogun is currently unable to take care of business on my behalf.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Alright then. I'll come out for a while.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Since the theme of the day is a change of pace, you can just call me Ei. I'm not a great fan of rigid titles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? But you're just Ei's consciousness, aren't you? Can consciousness actually leave this place?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I have my ways. I would never subject myself to imprisonment voluntarily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great. Then there's nothing to worry about! Allow us to be your tour guides!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Tour guides? What's a tour guide?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Someone to show you around the Inazuma of today and give you tips on where to eat and how to have fun! Alright, let's go go go!

choices.text: You haven't left in a long time, I'll bet?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: It's unnecessary, as far as I'm concerned. But since you are inviting me... a change of pace might well be nice.

choices.text: How about we go for a walk?
Seems a little arbitrary.
So it was all your doing.

talks.objective: Speak to Ei in the distance

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Your master shouldn't blame himself so much. Anyone else in his position would find it just as difficult to deal with.

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Exactly. He puts far too much pressure on himself...

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: *sigh*... The Kujou Clan's future isn't looking bright.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: She spends all her time alone. Having a visitor once in a while can't do any harm.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As the one who shook Eternity, you are her potential for change.

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: It's rumored that the Almighty Shogun has taken ill... Could it be true?

dialogues.speaker: Takeshi
dialogues.text: Ah, ignore me. Please, head in.
